description: The plot illustrates how model perplexity and GPU memory ratio vary as a function of the “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)” using two y-axes. The x-axis is labeled “Recent Sequence Ratio (%)”, appears linear, and spans roughly 10% to 100% with labeled ticks at 20, 40, 60, 80, and 100. The left y-axis is labeled “Perplexity”, linear, ranging from about 4.2 to 4.7 with ticks at 4.2, 4.3, 4.4, 4.5, 4.6, and 4.7, and includes a red dashed horizontal reference line near 4.38. The right y-axis is labeled “GPU Mem. Ratio (%)”, linear, ranging from about 40% to 100% with ticks at 40, 50, 60, 70, 80, 90, and 100, and includes a blue dashed horizontal reference line near 100% labeled “Full Cache GPU Mem.”. The perplexity series is an orange solid line with circular markers: it starts near 4.59 at 10%, decreases to about 4.45 at 20% and ~4.39 at 30%, reaches a low around 4.30 at 40%, rises to ~4.33–4.34 at 50–60%, dips to ~4.29 at 70%, then increases to ~4.33 at 80%, ~4.39 at 90%, and ends near ~4.38 at 100%. The GPU memory ratio series is a blue solid line with circular markers: it begins around 41% at 10% and increases gradually through ~42% (20%), ~43% (30%), ~44% (40%), ~45% (50%), ~46% (60%), ~48% (70%), and ~55% (80%), then jumps sharply to about ~98% at 90% and ends near ~99–100% at 100%.
